coded_because: GPIOx_IDR reads are impure (a function of the wired part/net, not stored SFR state) and GPIOx_BSRR writes mutate a SIBLING register (ODR) with BSx-over-BRx priority ordering -- both are read-purity violations per the design doc's data-vs-code rule (SS1, 'if every read is a pure function of stored state plus virtual time, and every write only stores, it is data; otherwise it is code'), and per the doc's whole-peripheral granularity ruling (SS1.8) the entire port routes to coded:, not just those two registers.
source: RM0490 Rev 6 Chapter 8 (General-purpose I/Os (GPIO)); STM32C031.svd peripheral GPIOA (GPIOB/C/D/F identical field layout at different base addresses)
verified: 2026-08-24. Same two-chain split as peripherals.stm32c0.rcc.json's reference case, applied honestly here rather than uniformly. (1) Bits/offsets: mechanically drafted from SVD. (2) Reset values: SVD-ONLY for every register in this file (MODER=0xEBFFFFFF, OTYPER/ODR/BSRR/AFRL=0x0, OSPEEDR=0x0C000000, PUPDR=0x24000000) -- hand-decoded bit-by-bit against each register's own field list to confirm internal SVD self-consistency (the same technique that caught RCC_CR's bug), and NONE of them contradicted their own field list the way CR did, but none was cross-checked against a SECOND independent source (no RM prose sentence or CMSIS default was found asserting these specific reset words, unlike RCC_CR's HSIDIV or FLASH_ACR's LATENCY/ICEN). Recorded as a real gap, not a false equivalence to RCC_CR's stronger corroboration. BSRR write semantics (ODR-mutation, BSx-over-BRx priority) and the MODER-before-drive requirement ARE independently verified against stm32c0xx_hal_gpio.c source (HAL_GPIO_WritePin/TogglePin), which is a behavioural check distinct from a reset-value check.

register_map.name: MODER
register_map.note: 2 bits/pin, 00=input 01=output 10=AF 11=analog. Reset value hand-decoded pin-by-pin: PA13/PA14=10(AF) so SWDIO/SWCLK stay live for debug with zero firmware init; every other GPIOA pin including PA5 (the LED) defaults to 11(analog). This is why HAL_GPIO_Init MUST run and set MODE5=01 before the LED does anything -- the single most likely 'nothing happens' bug in a from-scratch model.

register_map.name: OTYPER
register_map.note: 1 bit/pin, push-pull(0)/open-drain(1). Left at reset for both LED and USART2 TX in the BSP's default config.

register_map.name: OSPEEDR
register_map.note: 2 bits/pin slew rate. Not correctness-critical for a logic-level simulator; HAL writes it unconditionally so the class should still store it.

register_map.name: PUPDR
register_map.note: 2 bits/pin, 00=none 01=pull-up 10=pull-down. Relevant for PC13 (USER button) if it relies on an internal pull; relevant for USART2 RX if left floating.

register_map.name: IDR
register_map.note: READ-IMPURE. Must read the pin's net level from the wider part-wiring layer (the same SpareParts/pin-event mechanism webui/parts/ and webui/api.py's Pin already use per the design doc's SS3 rationale for putting GPIO in Python: 'a browser button press mutates IDR and raises EXTI via cm0_set_irq in one line'), not a value this class stores independently of ODR/MODER.

register_map.name: ODR
register_map.note: Plain storage, but HAL_GPIO_WritePin/TogglePin never write it directly -- see BSRR below. Still the value a read of an output pin returns, and BSRR writes are DEFINED in terms of what they do to ODR.

register_map.name: BSRR
register_map.note: WRITE-IMPURE, THE canonical coded register. VERIFIED against stm32c0xx_hal_gpio.c: HAL_GPIO_WritePin:421 'GPIOx->BSRR = (uint32_t)GPIO_Pin;' (set half) / reset half shifts into upper 16 bits; HAL_GPIO_TogglePin:470-473 reads ODR, XORs, writes BSRR from the result. SVD text confirms 'A read operation always returns 0x0000' and 'If both BSx and BRx are set, BSx h[as priority]'. The write handler must: never persist BSRR's own value (always reads 0), set the corresponding ODR bit for each BSy=1, clear the corresponding ODR bit for each BRy=1 UNLESS the matching BSy is also 1 (priority), and emit a pin-change event to the websocket per the design doc's SS3 rationale.

register_map.name: AFRL
register_map.note: 4 bits/pin (0-7). PA2/PA3 need AFSEL=0001 (GPIO_AF1_USART2, verified from nucleo-c031c6-bsp's COM1_TX_AF/COM1_RX_AF macros) for USART2 to actually appear on those pins -- without it the pin is AF-routed to the WRONG peripheral (AF0 default), a silent failure distinct from the GPIOAEN clock-gate false-green.

design_notes_for_the_python_class.rcc_dependency: Must consult RCC.IOPENR.<port>EN (see peripherals.stm32c0.rcc.json) before treating any write as observable -- if the port's clock is gated, MODER/BSRR writes should still store (matching real silicon, where the write doesn't fault) but must NOT emit a pin-change event, reproducing the 'false green' the survey warns about.
